summary: Show the loading splash earlier and open machine-data verification only when needed, preserving startup safety checks.
notes: The splash paints before machine-data checks and uses live white status text on its transparent background. An already-ready store opens under its configuration lock without briefly displaying the verification dialog.

Setup, migration, recovery, identity, receipt, deployment and authorization checks remain in place. Cancellation waits for a safe checkpoint and worker shutdown before locks are released; hardware-capable construction stays behind authorization on the GUI thread.

Large uploaded-design serialization and loading yield between rows using the existing worker control. Saving, fingerprints, source-file guards, allocation validation and publication interlocks retain their existing semantics. The 250 ms copy-heartbeat threshold is unchanged.
The simulated pressure-profile test waits for both chart targets before asserting convergence. No pressure command or firmware behavior changes.

The copy timing benchmark uses a fresh interpreter with normal GC and the unchanged workload, safety assertions and strict 250 ms limit. A full-suite run exposed 252-268 ms full-GC pauses on its accumulated test heap; arbitrary long-session GC latency remains unqualified.

Firmware artifact bytes and runtime dependencies are identical to v1.3.1. Machine-data schema, execution-calibration version 4 and both execution-data compatibility capabilities are unchanged. Existing installed-firmware provenance and SAFE requirements still apply.

Retains the three exact stable legacy migration cohorts and the separate pinned rc.11 release-candidate route. Legacy deployment retains its guarded migration, firmware/recovery verification and attended first-machine canary requirements.

Automatic rollback remains unconfigured. Preserve calibration measurements, committed counts, progress and immutable revisions; use protected current-version or exactly qualified compatible-bundle recovery.

See docs/v1.3.2_release_qualification.md for scope and evidence. Existing accepted large-optimizer timing limitations remain; this patch does not add physical-operation or long-session memory qualification.
